title: Slot
description: Parameters of a 'slot' operation (cam.h Operation::paramsJson, task T-055): centre-line slotting with a flat end mill as wide as the slot, one pass along the slot's centre line per depth, each depth entered by a zigzag ramp along the slot. The operation's geometry is the floor face of each slot: a centre line of lines and arcs swept by the slot's width, each end closed by a half circle or open (running out of the part). A tool narrower than the slot by more than the width tolerance is refused: machine such a slot as a 2D pocket. Its heights are measured from the top of the stock: 'clearance', 'retract' and 'feedPlane' as their names say, 'top' where the first depth starts; 'bottom' is not used (the floor is the slot's own, plus the floor stock). The cut feed is the cutting feed (Operation cutting feedCut), ramps use feedRamp and straight descents feedPlunge (0: the cutting feed). Lengths are millimetres, angles degrees. Annotations for editors: 'x-unit' (length, angle), 'x-propertyOrder' (the order of the form), 'x-heightsUsed' and 'x-cuttingUsed' (the members of the operation's heights and cutting data this type reads), 'x-geometry' (what the geometry picker selects: here faces) and 'x-toolTypes' (the tools the picker offers); docs/operation_types.md defines each.

x-geometry.description: Click the floor of each slot.

stepDown.title: Step down
stepDown.description: The most each depth goes below the one before; the depths are spread evenly from the top to the floor.

floorStock.title: Floor stock
floorStock.description: Material left on the slot's floor (the last depth stops this far above it).

rampAngle.title: Ramp angle
rampAngle.description: How steeply the tool ramps down into each depth, zigzagging along the slot.

minRampRun.title: Shortest ramp run
minRampRun.description: The shortest run along the slot a ramp may zigzag on; 0: the tool diameter. A slot whose centre line is shorter cannot be entered.

widthTolerance.title: Width tolerance
widthTolerance.description: How much narrower than the slot the tool may be (the slot then comes out as wide as the tool, with a warning). A tool wider than the slot is always refused.
